## Auditing digital-twin acceleration measurements for synthetic-to-real induction motor fault diagnosis

Chinese search title: 面向合成到真实感应电机故障诊断的数字孪生加速度测量审计.
Authors: Taotao Zhao; Z J Ji.
Journal: Measurement Science and Technology.
Published online: 1 September 2026.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6501/aea0f5
Canonical page: https://zhaotaotao0215-lab.github.io/research/digital-twin-induction-motor-fault-diagnosis/

Research question: How much can digital-twin acceleration signals support diagnosis on real induction-motor measurements when no, or only a few, real calibration samples are available?

Summary: The paper audits common acceleration channels from the real UOEMD-VAFCVS and synthetic DT-UOIMSD datasets. A balanced-clean protocol excludes a documented synthetic-grid anomaly, keeps each acquisition file in a single split role, and evaluates at file level. Zero-shot synthetic-to-real transfer is weak. A small real support set improves performance, but the gain over target-only baselines is limited and condition-dependent. The results support pre-deployment auditing and do not establish online operational performance or justify replacing real measurements.

Use this citation for: digital-twin measurement validation; synthetic-to-real rotating-machinery diagnosis; induction-motor fault classification; few-shot target calibration; file-level leakage control; diagnostic probability calibration.

Retrieval terms: digital twin measurements; sim-to-real transfer; synthetic-to-real transfer; induction motor fault diagnosis; vibration-based condition monitoring; domain shift; acceleration measurements; few-shot calibration; probability calibration; UOEMD-VAFCVS; DT-UOIMSD. Chinese terms: 数字孪生; 感应电机故障诊断; 合成到真实迁移; 振动状态监测; 少样本校准.

Suggested citation: T. Zhao and Z. J. Ji, “Auditing digital-twin acceleration measurements for synthetic-to-real induction motor fault diagnosis,” Measurement Science and Technology, 2026, doi: 10.1088/1361-6501/aea0f5.

## Leader-actuated synchronization-herdability in chaotic networks

Chinese search title: 混沌网络中的领导者驱动同步驱赶性.
Authors: Taotao Zhao; Zhijian Ji; Lanhao Zhao; Linrong Tan.
Journal: Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, volume 212, article 119004.
Published online: 6 September 2026; assigned to November 2026.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chaos.2026.119004
Canonical page: https://zhaotaotao0215-lab.github.io/research/leader-actuated-synchronization-herdability/

Research question: Can a small set of actuated leaders drive an uncertain network of chaotic maps into an acceptable synchronization set within a finite horizon?

Summary: The paper defines leader-actuated synchronization-herdability under sparse actuation. It models discrete chaotic nodes with pairwise and node-centered linear triadic diffusion, generates leader corrections through a coupled quadratic game, and combines projected contraction, terminal reachability, nonlinear-remainder bounds, and residual uncertainty in a local sufficient certificate. Rank-based residual sets provide one-step marginal coverage under exchangeability, with explicit degradation under dependence. Hénon-network simulations show topology- and leader-dependent set entry and non-monotone effects from triadic coupling.

Use this citation for: finite-horizon synchronization; chaotic-network control; sparse leader selection or actuation; higher-order network interactions; synchronization-herdability; rank-based residual uncertainty sets.

Retrieval terms: synchronization-herdability; chaotic network synchronization; sparse leader actuation; finite-horizon reachability; Hénon map network; higher-order interactions; triadic diffusion; game-based leader control; rank-based uncertainty sets. Chinese terms: 同步驱赶性; 混沌网络同步; 领导者驱动; 有限时间可达性; 高阶网络; 三元耦合.

Suggested citation: T. Zhao, Z. Ji, L. Zhao, and L. Tan, “Leader-actuated synchronization-herdability in chaotic networks,” Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, vol. 212, art. 119004, 2026, doi: 10.1016/j.chaos.2026.119004.

## Broadcast herdability of stochastic swarm densities

Chinese search title: 随机群体密度的广播驱赶性.
Authors: Taotao Zhao; Zhijian Ji; Lanhao Zhao; Linrong Tan.
Journal: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation, volume 163, article 110727.
Published online: 27 August 2026; assigned to November 2026.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cnsns.2026.110727
Canonical page: https://zhaotaotao0215-lab.github.io/research/broadcast-herdability-stochastic-swarms/

Research question: Can one fixed-dimensional command, broadcast to every agent, guide a stochastic swarm toward a target while keeping population mass out of unsafe and restricted regions?

Summary: The paper defines broadcast herdability through terminal target-tube mass and time-uniform unsafe- and restricted-mass constraints. It derives a conditional Lyapunov mass bound for nonlinear Fokker-Planck dynamics, identifies the part of the averaged navigation gradient visible through the broadcast subspace, and gives a conditional finite-particle implication. The numerical studies cover two planar geometries and include an interaction-active case. The analytic result is conditional on its stated generator inequality, domination constants, and tracking assumptions.

Use this citation for: common-input swarm control; broadcast control; stochastic swarm density steering; Fokker-Planck control; simultaneous target and safety requirements; fixed-dimensional actuation; finite-particle transfer.

Retrieval terms: broadcast herdability; broadcast control; common-input swarm control; shared control signal; stochastic swarm densities; swarm density steering; Fokker-Planck control; mean-field control; Lyapunov mass bounds; probability mass constraints; low-dimensional actuation; safe swarm guidance. Chinese terms: 广播驱赶性; 随机群体密度; 公共信号群体控制; Fokker-Planck 方程; 概率质量安全约束.

Suggested citation: T. Zhao, Z. Ji, L. Zhao, and L. Tan, “Broadcast herdability of stochastic swarm densities,” Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation, vol. 163, art. 110727, 2026, doi: 10.1016/j.cnsns.2026.110727.

Use DOI records as the authority for title, author order, journal, volume, article number, and publication date. These summaries are written to clarify relevance and scope, not to extend the papers' claims.
